title: On Restoring the old bridge in two years
subtitle: 艺术殿堂 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）
meta: 主题语境：艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）　|　核心词汇：restore　|　正文 354 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 restore 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 the grandmother ① restored the old bridge in two years in the rain, and every child in the courtyard said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the grandmother ② restores the old bridge in two years without complaint without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ restore the old bridge in two years at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ restored the old bridge in two years before — a line in the diary for February 1950 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Restoring the old bridge in two years in the rain, the grandmother said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the lamp at the far window, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ restore the field to its owner without complaint, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Restore the field to its owner at once and never mention it again.

By 1963 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the diary, and a new child from the next courtyard ⑧ restores the field to its owner in the rain every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the window, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ restored the old bridge in two years again when nobody else would.

⑩ To restore the old bridge in two years, my mother said in 1968, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the courtyard remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the courtyard forgets, somebody restores the old bridge in two years without complaint again and somebody must restore the old bridge in two years in the rain all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 修复（一般过去式 restored the old bridge in two years：1956 年祖母头一回这样做，淋着雨）
B. v. 修复（一般现在 restores the old bridge in two years：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 修复（不定式 to restore the old bridge in two years：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 修复（过去完成时 had restored the old bridge in two years：1950 年二月的日记上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 修复（动名词 restoring the old bridge in two years 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 归还（restore the field to its owner：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去归还把那块地归还给原主）
G. v. 归还（restore the field to its owner：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 修复（后段两处：新来的孩子照例 restores the field to its owner，而母亲又一次 restored the old bridge in two years）

answers.why: restore 意为“修复”，1956 年祖母淋着雨修复两年里修复了那座旧桥，那是院子里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 restored。
restore 意为“修复”，自那以后祖母毫无怨言地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 restores。
restore 意为“修复”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯修复两年里修复了那座旧桥”，此处为不定式 to restore the old bridge in two years。
restore 意为“修复”，日记里 二月 那行字说明早在 1963 年之前就有人修复过，故用过去完成时 had restored。
restore 意为“修复”，祖母说“修复两年里修复了那座旧桥这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 restoring the old bridge in two years 作主语。
restore 意为“归还”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去归还把那块地归还给原主”，should ever 之后用原形 restore the field to its owner。
restore 意为“归还”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻归还把那块地归还给原主（restore the field to its owner at once），以后再也不要提起。
restore 意为“修复”，新来的孩子每个年头都照例归还把那块地归还给原主，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 restores。
restore 意为“修复”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次淋着雨修复两年里修复了那座旧桥，用一般过去式 restored 叙述。
restore 意为“修复”，结尾那句是母亲 1968 年的话：要修复两年里修复了那座旧桥，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和院子记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 restore 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1956 the grandmother restored the old bridge in two years in the rain, and nobody in the courtyard forgot it.
Even now the grandmother restores the old bridge in two years without complaint whenever the courtyard asks.
Restoring the old bridge in two years in the rain, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever restore the field to its owner without complaint, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new child from the next courtyard restores the field to its owner in the rain every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother restored the old bridge in two years again, and the courtyard remembered that half.
